question: Can the continuous diffuse component of an independently Gaussian-perturbed lattice, multiplied by one positive developed-particle footprint, predict held historical photographic-film NPS bands better than both one-Gaussian and one-level Thomas-cluster controls?

primary_model_source.citation: Daniela Flimmel, Fitting regular point patterns with a hyperuniform perturbed lattice, revised March 22 2026; Stochastic Processes and their Applications 2026, 105037
primary_model_source.equation_basis: Lemma 2 decomposes the independently perturbed-lattice spectral measure into continuous 1-|phi_p(k)|^2 plus reciprocal-lattice Bragg atoms; for isotropic Gaussian displacement phi_p gives the continuous factor 1-exp(-sigma_squared*angular_frequency_squared)
primary_model_source.source_limit: The paper studies metallic polycrystal centres, not photographic emulsion, and reports that the independent model can retain restrictive Bragg peaks; only its continuous repulsive baseline is tested here.

branch_rule.pass: Retain the diffuse repulsive-point baseline only as historical measured-NPS compatibility and open a separately frozen finite-field/Bragg-atom falsification before any image use.
branch_rule.fail: Close this exact independent perturbed-lattice diffuse family without adding dependent fields, Bragg smoothing, capacity or same-cohort gate changes; advance a new measured observation or mechanism.
branch_rule.always: Never identify lattice spacing, crystal centres or photographic-emulsion hyperuniformity from this compatibility test.

forbidden: inspect confirmation bands before candidate and controls freeze
fit or smooth Bragg atoms after seeing the measured spectra
reuse a dependent perturbation field as a rescue
interpret fitted particle or jitter sigmas as microscopic measurements
density interpolation, photographic rendering, modern-stock or product claims
claim_ceiling: Held-band compatibility of one 2026 paper-derived continuous repulsive-point structure factor with five historical Fuji B&W measured spectra; not evidence of photographic-emulsion hyperuniformity, microscopic lattice geometry, modern stock or product quality.
